topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the course structure, the lecturer, and the core learning outcomes on cancer etiology.

topics.label: Foundational concepts and epidemiological evidence of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual basis of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous biological errors and inherited predispositions with environmental exposures and population-level epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens as drivers of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral and bacterial pathogens contribute to cancer development, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a primary mechanistic case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, radiation, and metabolic byproducts induce direct DNA damage, adducts, and mutational transversions.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental stages of vulnerability in cancer pathogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for determining and proving carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomics, biobanking, animal models, and in vitro assays used to identify carcinogens and validate their cancer-causing mechanisms.

topics.label: Summary and risk-benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with framing on everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding carcinogens before closing the session.
